## What

Write `docs/adr/0101-*.md` amending ADR 0043. ADR 0043 itself is NOT edited — it is a historical
record, and ADR 0061 already set the precedent of amending it rather than rewriting.

## Must record

- Why `operator` mis-signalled: it means a human throughout this repo, so agents inferred a
  person was required, when an agent recording a Gerrit vote attests equally well.
- Why `[non-codebase]`: it is the missing half of a pair the vocabulary already had. The
  `[codebase]` token is already recognized at exactly three sites — `docs/adr/0043-...md:45`
  ("anything else — untagged, an explicit `[codebase]`, or a malformed near-miss"),
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md:95`, and
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_evidence_kind.md:56`. (It is NOT in
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`, which uses the category name
  `codebase-verifiable` rather than the bracket tag — the two are different vocabularies and the
  ADR must not conflate them.) `[codebase]` is prompt-level only: no regex parses it.
  `[non-codebase]` also resists attestation laundering by construction — to tag a criterion whose
  proof is `tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py`, an author must assert that file is "non-codebase",
  which is self-evidently false.
- Why `attested` alone was rejected: `SOURCE_ATTESTED = "attested"` is the snapshot gate
  read-root mode meaning "pinned to an immutable in-repo SHA" — near-opposite sense, same
  readers, though no functional conflict.
- That `[operator-attested]` remains accepted and is deliberately UNDOCUMENTED, because 827 of
  4,285 live tickets carry it in immutable event records.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] ADR 0101 exists, is Accepted, and records the four points above.
- [x] ADR 0043 is unmodified.
- [x] `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py` run; `docs/adr/README.md` and `docs/adr/.numbers/` updated.
- [x] `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` and `scripts/check_docs_index.py` pass.
